title: How would you like to pay
paragraphs: How do you pay for your coffee? Is it with change? I use my tap-and-go card. I don't even need to enter my PIN number or a signature to authorise payment. It's quicker and everybody in the queue is happy.

Contactless payments are gaining popularity. Those concerned about security will be pleased to know that the amount of money you can spend in one go is limited - in the UK it's currently £30. But if the card is used a few times in a row, a PIN number will be needed. If a thief gets hold of your card and goes on a spending spree, your bank covers you against fraud. Whereas, if someone steals your banknotes, that's your bad luck!

For those who are always forgetting where they put their cards, there's a new solution: wearable tech: clothing and accessories that have integrated electronic technology. Kenneth Cukier, an economist and technology expert, says: "You can simply take any wireless card and the chip from it that your bank might issue you with, and you can put it in a coat. When you want to make a payment just wave your arm in front of the terminal and leave the coffee shop with your latte. This is intended for people who don't want to take their card out of their wallet, use their phone or their watch."

Good, isn't it? And new ways of spending money are not stopping there. The future is all about biometrics. Very convenient if you are at the beach or a festival - there's a new system in development which will make it possible to read the unique maps of veins under the surface of your finger, and use them to authenticate payments - or prove that it's you making the payments. You just need to remember which finger you registered with.

So spending money is becoming easier all the time. And the temptation to buy more stuff increases. But it's worth bearing in mind that earning the money in the first place will still require the same effort. Back to work then!

vocabulary.entry: tap-and-go card [n.] /tæp ənd ɡəʊ kɑːd/ 非接触式支付卡 (固定搭配；专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Tap-and-go cards make paying for small purchases quick and easy.
vocabulary.translation: 非接触式支付卡让小额购物付款快捷方便。

vocabulary.entry: PIN number [n.] /pɪn ˈnʌmbə/ 个人识别码 (专业词汇；缩写)
vocabulary.example: You will need to enter your PIN number to complete the transaction.
vocabulary.translation: 你需要输入个人识别码来完成交易。

vocabulary.entry: authorise [v.] /ˈɔːθəraɪz/ 授权；批准 (书面语；英式拼写，美式: authorize)
vocabulary.example: The bank authorised the payment after checking his account.
vocabulary.translation: 银行核实他的账户后批准了这笔付款。

vocabulary.entry: in one go [phr.] /ɪn wʌn ɡəʊ/ 一口气；一下子 (固定搭配；口语)
vocabulary.example: He paid the whole bill in one go.
vocabulary.translation: 他一次性付清了全部账单。

vocabulary.entry: in a row [phr.] /ɪn ə rəʊ/ 连续；成一排 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: She won the competition for the third year in a row.
vocabulary.translation: 她连续第三年赢得了比赛。

vocabulary.entry: get hold of [phr.] /ɡet həʊld əv/ 抓住；得到；找到 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: I need to get hold of a copy of that report.
vocabulary.translation: 我需要弄到那份报告的一份副本。

vocabulary.entry: spending spree [n.] /ˈspendɪŋ spriː/ 疯狂消费；大肆挥霍 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: After winning the lottery, he went on a spending spree.
vocabulary.translation: 中彩票后，他开始大肆挥霍。

vocabulary.entry: cover against [phr.] /ˈkʌvər əˈɡenst/ 为……提供保险；承担……损失 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The insurance policy covers you against theft and loss.
vocabulary.translation: 这份保险单为你提供盗窃和损失保障。

vocabulary.entry: fraud [n.] /frɔːd/ 欺诈；诈骗 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: He was found guilty of credit card fraud.
vocabulary.translation: 他被判犯有信用卡欺诈罪。

vocabulary.entry: wearable tech [n.] /ˈweərəbl tek/ 可穿戴技术 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Wearable tech such as smartwatches is becoming increasingly popular.
vocabulary.translation: 智能手表等可穿戴技术正变得越来越流行。

vocabulary.example: She bought a handbag and other accessories to match her outfit.
vocabulary.translation: 她买了一个手提包和其他配饰来搭配她的衣服。

vocabulary.entry: integrate [v.] /ˈɪntɪɡreɪt/ 使合并；使融入；使一体化 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The new system integrates data from multiple sources.
vocabulary.translation: 新系统整合了来自多个来源的数据。

vocabulary.example: Please swipe your card at the payment terminal.

vocabulary.entry: biometrics [n.] /ˌbaɪəʊˈmetrɪks/ 生物识别技术 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Biometrics is increasingly used for security and identification.
vocabulary.translation: 生物识别技术越来越多地用于安全和身份识别。

vocabulary.example: The nurse inserted the needle into a vein in his arm.
vocabulary.translation: 护士将针头插入他手臂的静脉。

vocabulary.entry: authenticate [v.] /ɔːˈθentɪkeɪt/ 验证；证实 (专业词汇；书面语)
vocabulary.example: You need to authenticate your identity using your fingerprint.
vocabulary.translation: 你需要使用指纹验证身份。

vocabulary.example: He couldn't resist the temptation to buy another pair of shoes.
vocabulary.translation: 他无法抵抗再买一双鞋的诱惑。

vocabulary.entry: bear in mind [phr.] /beər ɪn maɪnd/ 记住；考虑到 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Bear in mind that prices may change without notice.
vocabulary.translation: 记住价格可能随时变动，恕不另行通知。
